Sometimes too the justice of God is taken for befittingness [that is, what befits God's own goodness, not what is owed to the creature], by which it befits him to act in this way or that: and so the acts of the divine kindness are just, because God is so good that it befits him to work mercifully, and to pardon some, and to repay good for evil. Hence the Psalmist says: [[Ps 24:10|All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth|Universæ viæ Domini misericordia et veritas]]. And again: [[Ps 144:17|The Lord is just in all his ways|Justus Dominus in omnibus viis suis]]. In this sense Azarias, standing unhurt in the midst of the burning furnace[[Dan 3:25||]], said: [[Dan 3:27|Thou art just|Justus es]], [[Dan 3:26|O Lord, the God of our fathers|Domine, Deus patrum nostrorum]], [[Dan 3:27|in all that thou hast done to us, and all thy works are true, and thy ways right|in omnibus quæ fecisti nobis, et universa opera tua vera, et viæ tuæ rectæ]]: as is found in Daniel.

paras.t: Et nunc, Domine, memor esto mei, id est, per exauditionem gratiosam ostende te memorem esse mei, qui nunquam tuorum oblivisceris, et ne vindictam sumas de peccatis meis. Ecce quanta humilitas justi istius, qui cuncta quæ toleravit, non reputavit condigna aut sufficientia esse flagella culparum suarum, imo graviora se fatebatur promeruisse, a quibus petiit misericorditer erui. Neque reminiscaris delicta mea vel parentum meorum, id est, per effectum justæ ultionis non ostendas te reminisci peccata nostra, sed ea clementer remittas quasi non fuerint, et reminiscere miserationum tuarum. Denique specialiter orat pro suis parentibus, qui forsan in brevi defuncti fuerunt, vel adhuc vivebant. Et quamvis (sicut in præcedenti habetur capitulo) parentes ipsius irridebant eum, ipse nihilo minus orat tota devotione pro illis: siquidem filii parentibus suis æquivalens reddere nequeunt.
paras.en: [[3:3|And now, O Lord, think of me|Et nunc, Domine, memor esto mei]] [literally "be mindful of me", which the gloss takes up], that is, by graciously hearing me show that thou art mindful of me, thou who never forgettest thine own; [[3:3|and take not revenge of my sins|et ne vindictam sumas de peccatis meis]]. See how great was the humility of this just man, who did not reckon all that he had endured to be scourges worthy of his faults, or sufficient for them; nay, he confessed that he had deserved heavier ones, from which he asked to be mercifully delivered. [[3:3|neither remember my offences, nor those of my parents|Neque reminiscaris delicta mea vel parentum meorum]], that is, do not show by the effect of just vengeance that thou rememberest our sins, but mercifully remit them as though they had never been, and [[Ps 24:6|Remember, O Lord, thy bowels of compassion|reminiscere miserationum tuarum]] [the margin gives Ps. xxiv; Denis's words, *reminiscere miserationum tuarum*, "remember thy mercies", are from Ps 24:6]. Lastly, he prays especially for his parents, who perhaps had died a short while before, or were still living. And although (as is found in the preceding chapter) his parents mocked him[[Tob 2:15||]] [*parentes* means both parents and kinsfolk; at Tob 2:15 the word stands beside *cognati*, kinsmen], he none the less prays for them with all devotion: since children cannot repay their parents in equal measure.

paras.t: Quoniam non obedivimus præceptis tuis. Non pro propria persona hoc ait, quia jam patuit, quod in cunctis obedivit divinis præceptis; sed in persona peccatorum et transgressorum, quibus se ex humilitate connumerat, tanquam unus ex populo illo. Juxta quem modum loquitur Isaias, dicendo: Nos reputavimus eum quasi leprosum et percussum a Deo. Esdras quoque et Daniel in orationibus suis dixerunt: Deus meus, confundor et erubesco levare faciem meam ad te, quoniam iniquitates nostræ multiplicatæ sunt super caput nostrum, et delicta nostra creverunt usque ad cœlum. Ideo traditi sumus in direptionem, id est, bona nostra temporalia ablata sunt nobis; et captivitatem, id est, in personis propriis per captivitatem puniti sumus; et mortem: unde dictum est supra, quod Sennacherib multos ex captivis occidit; et in fabulam et in improperium omnibus nationibus, scilicet Persis, Medis, Assyriis, in quibus dispersisti nos; quæ de nostris calamitatibus inter se fabulantur, et nobis assidue convitiantur. Secundum quod in Jeremia Dominus ait de talibus: Dabo eos in vexationem et maledictionem, et in stuporem et in sibilum, et in opprobrium, eo quod non audierint verba mea.
paras.en: [[3:4|For we have not obeyed thy commandments|Quoniam non obedivimus præceptis tuis]]. He does not say this in his own person, since it has already been shown that he obeyed the divine commandments in all things; but in the person of sinners and transgressors, among whom he numbers himself out of humility, as one of that people. In the same manner Isaias speaks, saying: [[Is 53:4|we have thought him as it were a leper, and as one struck by God|Nos reputavimus eum quasi leprosum et percussum a Deo]]. Esdras too and Daniel[[Dan 3:30||]] [the margin's reference for Daniel is hard to read and seems to end in 30: perhaps Dan 3:30, in the prayer of Azarias, "we have not hearkened to thy commandments"; Daniel's own confession is at Dan 9:5] said in their prayers: [[1 Esd 9:6|My God I am confounded and ashamed to lift up my face to thee: for our iniquities are multiplied over our heads, and our sins are grown up even unto heaven|Deus meus, confundor et erubesco levare faciem meam ad te, quoniam iniquitates nostræ multiplicatæ sunt super caput nostrum, et delicta nostra creverunt usque ad cœlum]]. [[3:4|therefore are we delivered to spoil|Ideo traditi sumus in direptionem]], that is, our temporal goods have been taken from us; [[3:4|and to captivity|et captivitatem]], that is, we have been punished in our own persons by captivity; [[3:4|and death|et mortem]]: whence it was said above that Sennacherib slew many of the captives[[Tob 1:21||]]; [[3:4|and are made a fable, and a reproach to all nations|et in fabulam et in improperium omnibus nationibus]], namely the Persians, Medes and Assyrians, [[3:4|amongst which thou hast scattered us|in quibus dispersisti nos]]; who make fables among themselves of our calamities [*fabulantur*, from *fabula*, the "fable" of the verse], and constantly revile us. As the Lord says in Jeremias of such men: [[Jer 29:18|I will give them up unto affliction|Dabo eos in vexationem]] and [[Jer 29:18|to be a curse, and an astonishment, and a hissing, and a reproach|maledictionem, et in stuporem et in sibilum, et in opprobrium]], [[Jer 29:19|Because they have not hearkened to my words|eo quod non audierint verba mea]].

paras.t: Et nunc, Domine, magna judicia tua, id est justa et sancta ac irreprehensibilia, quia non egimus secundum præcepta tua, et non ambulavimus sinceriter coram te, id est pura ac recta intentione: quia etsi bona aliqua egimus, tamen multis malis admixta fuerunt, nec satis sincera fuit intentio nostra, quia ad propria commoda reflexi exstitimus, vel ad laudes humanas; et ita quasi pannus menstruatæ sunt universæ justitiæ nostræ.
paras.en: [[3:5|And now, O Lord, great are thy judgments|Et nunc, Domine, magna judicia tua]], that is, just and holy and irreproachable, [[3:5|because we have not done according to thy precepts|quia non egimus secundum præcepta tua]], [[3:5|and have not walked sincerely before thee|et non ambulavimus sinceriter coram te]], that is, with a pure and right intention: for even if we have done some good things, yet they were mixed with many evils, nor was our intention sincere enough, since we were turned back upon our own advantage, or upon human praise; and so [[Is 64:6|all our justices as the rag of a menstruous woman|quasi pannus menstruatæ sunt universæ justitiæ nostræ]].

paras.t: Et nunc, Domine, secundum voluntatem tuam, id est spontaneam tuam pietatem, fac mecum: juxta illud Psalmi: Benigne fac, Domine, in bona voluntate tua Sion: et præcipe in pace recipi spiritum meum, id est, animam meam jube angelico ministerio tolli a corpore, et quiete transferri ad limbum patrum, sinumve Abrahæ, id est ad secretam requiem illam et pacem, in qua fuit certa exspectatio æternæ salutis, et quies ab omni præsentis vitæ tumultu. Sic et justus Simeon dixit: Nunc dimittis servum tuum, Domine, secundum verbum tuum in pace.
paras.en: [[3:6|And now, O Lord|Et nunc, Domine]], [[3:6|according to thy will|secundum voluntatem tuam]], that is, according to thy own free kindness, [[3:6|do with me|fac mecum]]: according to that of the Psalm: [[Ps 50:20|Deal favourably, O Lord, in thy good will with Sion|Benigne fac, Domine, in bona voluntate tua Sion]]; [[3:6|and command my spirit to be received in peace|et præcipe in pace recipi spiritum meum]], that is, command my soul to be taken from the body by the ministry of angels, and to be borne quietly to the limbo of the fathers, or Abraham's bosom, that is, to that hidden rest and peace in which there was the sure expectation of eternal salvation, and rest from all the tumult of the present life. So too the just Simeon said: [[Luke 2:29|Now thou dost dismiss thy servant, O Lord, according to thy word in peace|Nunc dimittis servum tuum, Domine, secundum verbum tuum in pace]]

paras.t: Expedit enim mihi mori magis quam vivere. Hoc aliquo modo sic fuit secundum considerationem Tobiæ: quia utilius fuit ei in sinu Abrahæ repausare, quam assidue sic affligi, et periculis peccandi exponi, quia ex sua cæcitate, irrisione, paupertate, aliisque adversis poterat paulatim ad impatientiam aut inordinatam labi tristitiam. Verumtamen absolute loquendo, salubrius fuit ei et aliis manere et conservari in vita eo modo, quo Deus decrevit eum conservare in vita hac per gratiam et profectum virtutum, atque per reductionem ad temporalem ac spiritualem prosperitatem eximiam, secundum quod infra habetur. Denique, juxta hunc modum leguntur sancti viri interdum mortem optasse, et pro ea orasse, non ex impatientia, sed cautela et desiderio vitæ quietioris: tamen occasione magnæ adversitatis et afflictionis: a qua secundum divinæ voluntatis pietatem velle liberari, non videtur peccatum. Sic namque Moyses ait ad Dominum: Non possum solus sustinere omnem hunc populum, quia gravis est mihi. Sin aliter tibi videtur, obsecro ut interficias me, et inveniam gratiam in oculis tuis, ne tantis afficiar malis. Sic et Elias fugiens impiissimam Jezabel, legitur exorasse: Sufficit mihi, Domine, tolle (quæso) animam meam. Apostolus quoque: Supra modum, inquit, gravati sumus supra virtutem, ita ut tæderet nos vivere.
paras.en: [[3:6|for it is better for me to die, than to live|Expedit enim mihi mori magis quam vivere]]. In a certain way this was so, as Tobias considered it: since it was more profitable for him to rest in Abraham's bosom than to be afflicted so continually, and exposed to dangers of sinning, for through his blindness, the mockery, his poverty and other adversities he could little by little slip into impatience or inordinate sadness. Yet absolutely speaking, it was more wholesome for him and for others that he should remain and be kept in life in the way in which God decreed to keep him in this life, through grace and progress in the virtues, and through his being brought back to an outstanding temporal and spiritual prosperity, as is found below. Lastly, in this way holy men are read at times to have wished for death and prayed for it, not out of impatience, but out of caution and the desire of a quieter life: yet on the occasion of great adversity and affliction; and to wish to be delivered from this, in accordance with the kindness of the divine will, does not seem to be a sin. For so Moses said to the Lord: [[Num 11:14|I am not able alone to bear all this people, because it is too heavy for me.|Non possum solus sustinere omnem hunc populum, quia gravis est mihi]] [[Num 11:15|But if it seem unto thee otherwise, I beseech thee to kill me, and let me find grace in thy eyes, that I be not afflicted with so great evils.|Sin aliter tibi videtur, obsecro ut interficias me, et inveniam gratiam in oculis tuis, ne tantis afficiar malis]][[Deut 1:12||]] [the margin also gives Deut. i, with numerals hard to read: Moses says much the same at Deut 1:9–12] So too Elias, fleeing the most wicked Jezabel, is read to have prayed: [[3 Kings 19:4|It is enough for me, Lord|Sufficit mihi, Domine]], [[3 Kings 19:4|take away|tolle]] (I pray) [[3 Kings 19:4|my soul|animam meam]]. The Apostle too: [[2 Cor 1:8|we were pressed out of measure|Supra modum]], he says, [[2 Cor 1:8|above our strength, so that we were weary even of life|gravati sumus supra virtutem, ita ut tæderet nos vivere]].

paras.t: Eadem die qua sic oravit Tobias, contigit ut Sara filia Raguelis, Israelitæ capti et habitantis in Rages civitate Medorum, audiret improperium ab una ex ancillis patris sui, a qua potius debuit honorari: et gravius fuit a vili et subjecta persona sic objurgari; quoniam tradita fuit septem viris a suis parentibus successive. Nec certum est, an viri illi fuerunt gentiles idololatræ, aut ex filiis Israel captis. Et quidquid inde dicatur, constat quod viri illi fuerunt iniqui, et tam virtuosæ puellæ conjugio et amplexu indigni. Nam et Israelitæ captivi, pro maxima parte fuerunt idololatræ. Sed quoniam infra Raguel ait, Credo quod ideo fecit vos Dominus venire ad me, ut ista conjungeretur cognationi suæ secundum legem Moysis, ad minus elicitur, quod viri illi non erant de tribu Raguelis et Saræ, sicut Tobias.
paras.en: [[3:7|Now it happened on the same day|Eadem die]] on which Tobias prayed thus, [[3:7|that Sara daughter of Raguel|contigit ut Sara filia Raguelis]], an Israelite captive dwelling [[3:7|in Rages a city of the Medes|in Rages civitate Medorum]], [[3:7|received a reproach from one of her father's servant maids|audiret improperium ab una ex ancillis patris sui]], by whom she ought rather to have been honoured: and it was the harder to be so rebuked by a base and subject person; [[3:8|Because she had been given to seven husbands|quoniam tradita fuit septem viris]] by her parents, one after another. Nor is it certain whether those husbands were idolatrous gentiles, or of the captive children of Israel. And whatever be said of this, it is clear that those men were wicked, and unworthy of the marriage and embrace of so virtuous a maiden. For the captive Israelites too were for the most part idolaters. But since Raguel says below: [[Tob 7:14|I believe he hath therefore made you come to me, that this maid might be married to one of her own kindred, according to the law of Moses|Credo quod ideo fecit vos Dominus venire ad me, ut ista conjungeretur cognationi suæ secundum legem Moysis]], it follows at least that those men were not of the tribe of Raguel and Sara, as Tobias was[[Num 36:8||]].

paras.t: Et dæmonium, nomine Asmodæus, occiderat eos, non sine permissione divina atque angelica. Erant quippe iniqui et libidinosi, ideo morte digni: sicque dæmon fuit exsecutor divinæ justitiæ in illorum punitione, quemadmodum in adolescentis occisione, qui sanctam Agnetem volebat polluere. Mox ut ingressi fuissent ad eam in cubile aut lectum, antequam eam cognoverant.
paras.en: [[3:8|and a devil named Asmodeus had killed them|Et dæmonium, nomine Asmodæus, occiderat eos]], not without divine and angelic permission. For they were wicked and lustful, and so deserving of death: and thus the devil was the executor of divine justice in punishing them, as in the slaying of the youth who wished to defile Saint Agnes [in the Acts of St Agnes, the prefect's son who tried to violate her was struck dead by a devil]. [[3:8|at their first going in unto her|Mox ut ingressi fuissent ad eam]], into the bedchamber or bed, before they had known her.

paras.t: Ergo quum pro culpa sua increparet puellam ex caritate et zelo justitiæ, quoniam justa fuit et fervida, respondit ei puella illa impatiens et perversa, dicens: Amplius non, id est nunquam in posterum, videamus ex te filium aut filiam super terram, hoc est, sterilis maneas, sicut hucusque fuisti, Interfectrix virorum tuorum. Sicque false accusavit Saram de tanto facinore, imo et facinoris tanti tam frequenti reiteratione. Malevole quoque maledixit eidem, imprecando ei sterilitatem, quæ tunc fuit grande opprobrium. Hujus perversæ puellæ pravitatem impatientiamque sectantur multi, superbi, duri, impatientes, qui juste reprehensi, non solum non recognoscunt propriam culpam, sed in ipsum invehuntur corripientem: quem si vere reprehendere nequeunt, criminantur eum mendaciter. De quibus scripsit Amos: Odio habuerunt corripientem, et perfecte loquentem abominati sunt. Ecclesiasticus quoque: Peccator vitabit omnem correptionem. Verum (ut Salomon protestatur) qui increpationes relinquit, insipiens est; et qui impatiens est, operatur stultitiam.
paras.en: [[3:9|So when she reproved the maid for her fault|Ergo quum pro culpa sua increparet puellam]] out of charity and zeal for justice, since she was just and fervent, [[3:9|she answered her|respondit ei]], that impatient and perverse maid, [[3:9|saying|dicens]]: [[3:9|May we never|Amplius non]], that is, never hereafter, [[3:9|see son, or daughter of thee upon the earth|videamus ex te filium aut filiam super terram]], that is, mayest thou remain barren, as thou hast been until now, [[3:9|thou murderer of thy husbands|Interfectrix virorum tuorum]]. And so she falsely accused Sara of so great a crime, nay, of so frequent a repetition of so great a crime. She also cursed her malevolently, wishing barrenness upon her, which was then a great reproach. The depravity and impatience of this perverse maid are copied by many, proud, hard and impatient men, who when justly reproved not only do not acknowledge their own fault, but inveigh against the very one who corrects them: and if they cannot truly reprove him, they accuse him falsely. Of whom Amos wrote: [[Amos 5:10|They have hated him that rebuketh|Odio habuerunt corripientem]], [[Amos 5:10|and have abhorred him that speaketh perfectly|et perfecte loquentem abominati sunt]]. Ecclesiasticus too: [[Ecclus 32:21|A sinful man will flee reproof|Peccator vitabit omnem correptionem]] [the margin's reading is unclear (Eccli. xxxi?); the words are those of Ecclus 32:21, where Denis has "every reproof"]. But (as Solomon declares) [[Prov 10:17|he that forsaketh reproofs|qui increpationes relinquit]] [[Prov 12:1|is foolish|insipiens est]]; and [[Prov 14:29|he that is impatient|qui impatiens est]] [[Prov 14:17|shall work folly|operatur stultitiam]] [Denis joins Prov 10:17 with 12:1, and 14:29 with 14:17, as the margin indicates].

paras.t: Numquid et me occidere vis, sicut occidisti septem viros? Tanta est iniquorum, iracundorum, superborum, impatientiumque perversitas, excæcatio, ingratitudo, ut justam et caritativam correptionem (quæ est beneficium maximum) arbitrentur summam injuriam, maleficium, et quasi impetitionem ad mortem. Merito igitur scriptum est: Sapientiam et disciplinam qui abjicit, infelix est.
paras.en: [[3:10|Wilt thou kill me also|Numquid et me occidere vis]], [[3:10|as thou hast already killed seven husbands?|sicut occidisti septem viros?]] So great is the perversity, blindness and ingratitude of the wicked, the wrathful, the proud and the impatient, that they reckon a just and charitable correction (which is the greatest of kindnesses) the highest injury, an evil deed, and as it were an assault unto death. Rightly therefore is it written: [[Wis 3:11|he that rejecteth wisdom, and discipline, is unhappy|Sapientiam et disciplinam qui abjicit, infelix est]].

paras.t: Ad hanc vocem perrexit in superius cubiculum domus suæ; in quo sibi forsan oratorium præparavit, quemadmodum Judith, quatenus in loco illo secreto, quieto et alto, devotioni, contemplationi, orationi liberius puriusque vacaret. Denique sapiens virgo Sara noluit cum impudenti et perversa ancilla contendere, nec ei dure quid respondere, cernens eam incorrigibilem esse; sciens verum esse quod Salomon dixit: Honor est homini qui separat se a contentionibus.
paras.en: [[3:10|At these words, she went into an upper chamber of her house|Ad hanc vocem perrexit in superius cubiculum domus suæ]]; in which perhaps she had prepared an oratory for herself, as Judith did[[Jdt 8:5||]], so that in that secret, quiet and high place she might give herself more freely and purely to devotion, contemplation and prayer. Further, the wise virgin Sara would not quarrel with the shameless and perverse maid, nor answer her anything harshly, seeing that she was incorrigible; knowing that what Solomon said is true: [[Prov 20:3|It is an honour for a man to separate himself from quarrels|Honor est homini qui separat se a contentionibus]].

paras.t: Et tribus diebus et noctibus non manducavit neque bibit; sed in oratione persistens, cum lacrimis deprecabatur Deum, ut ab isto improperio liberaret eam, id est, a tanta diffamia eam eriperet, ne alii scandalizarentur in ea, et veritas ad Dei honorem pateret, et ipsa de cetero efficeretur fecunda. Præterea an toto triduo ex devotione atque fervore absque interruptione oraverit, nec quidquam cibi et potus ac somni acceperit, an potius ideo dicatur infra tres dies et noctes orasse, et nil cibi ac potus sumpsisse, quia pro majori parte temporis illius oravit, et permodicum de cibo accepit et potu, videtur incertum. Utroque etenim modo potest intelligi, quia quod modicum est, reputatur pro nihilo. Nam et in Actibus legitur, Paulum dixisse quibusdam in navi: Quartadecima die hodie exspectantes, jejuni permanetis, nihil accipientes.
paras.en: [[3:10|and for three days and three nights did neither eat nor drink|Et tribus diebus et noctibus non manducavit neque bibit]]; [[3:11|But continuing in prayer with tears besought God|sed in oratione persistens, cum lacrimis deprecabatur Deum]], [[3:11|that he would deliver her from this reproach|ut ab isto improperio liberaret eam]], that is, that he would snatch her from so great a defamation, lest others should be scandalized in her, and that the truth might be made plain to the honour of God, and she herself be made fruitful from then on. Moreover, whether for the whole three days she prayed without interruption out of devotion and fervour, and took nothing at all of food and drink and sleep, or whether she is rather said to have prayed during three days and nights, and to have taken nothing of food and drink, because she prayed for the greater part of that time, and took very little of food and drink, seems uncertain. For it can be understood either way, since what is little is reckoned as nothing. For in the Acts too we read that Paul said to certain men in the ship: [[Acts 27:33|This day is the fourteenth day that you have waited and continued fasting, taking nothing|Quartadecima die hodie exspectantes, jejuni permanetis, nihil accipientes]].

paras.t: Factum est autem tertia die, dum compleret orationem, benedicens Dominum benedictione laudis, qua inferior benedicit superiori. De benedictione vero consecrationis, ait ad Hebræos Apostolus: Sine ulla contradictione, quod minus est, a majore benedicitur. Dicit: Benedictum est nomen tuum, id est, tu ipse nomine nominante designatus, es benedictus, Deus patrum nostrorum. Sæpissime etenim in Scripturis accipitur nomen rei pro re ipsa, quemadmodum et in Oratione dominica: Sanctificetur nomen tuum. Itaque venerabilis Sara, ex tam diuturna et ferventi oratione desuper intra se secrete consolata, et spe exauditionis exhilarata, Dominum benedixit.
paras.en: [[3:12|And it came to pass on the third day when she was making an end of her prayer|Factum est autem tertia die, dum compleret orationem]], [[3:12|blessing the Lord|benedicens Dominum]] with the blessing of praise, by which the lesser blesses the greater. But of the blessing of consecration the Apostle says to the Hebrews: [[Heb 7:7|without all contradiction, that which is less is blessed by the better|Sine ulla contradictione, quod minus est, a majore benedicitur]]. [[3:13|She said|Dicit]]: [[3:13|Blessed is thy name|Benedictum est nomen tuum]], that is, thou thyself, who art signified by the name that names thee, art blessed, [[3:13|O God of our fathers|Deus patrum nostrorum]]. For very often in the Scriptures the name of a thing is taken for the thing itself, as also in the Lord's Prayer: [[Matt 6:9|hallowed be thy name|Sanctificetur nomen tuum]]. So the venerable Sara, secretly comforted within herself from above after so long and fervent a prayer, and gladdened by the hope of being heard, blessed the Lord.

paras.t: Qui quum iratus fueris, non per invariabilis mentis tuæ commotionem, aut per tuæ infinitæ tranquillitatis perturbationem, sed per justæ ultionis effectum, misericordiam facies: quia per pœnas temporales ignoscis contritis, et citra condignum punis; et in tempore tribulationis peccata dimittis his qui invocant te, qui tuæ pietatis flagella patienter atque humiliter amplectuntur, confitentes multo duriora promeruisse, ac misericorditer sibi indulgeri petentes. Sic et Habacuc asserit: Quum iratus fueris, misericordiæ recordaberis. Et Psalmista: Aut obliviscetur misereri Deus, aut continebit in ira sua misericordias suas?
paras.en: [[3:13|who when thou hast been angry|Qui quum iratus fueris]], not by any change in thy unchangeable mind, nor by any disturbance of thy infinite tranquillity, but by the effect of just vengeance, [[3:13|wilt shew mercy|misericordiam facies]]: since by temporal punishments thou pardonest the contrite, and punishest them less than they deserve; [[3:13|and in the time of tribulation forgivest the sins of them that call upon thee|et in tempore tribulationis peccata dimittis his qui invocant te]], who embrace the scourges of thy kindness patiently and humbly, confessing that they have deserved far harder ones, and asking that they be mercifully forgiven. So too Habacuc declares: [[Hab 3:2|when thou art angry, thou wilt remember mercy|Quum iratus fueris, misericordiæ recordaberis]]. And the Psalmist: [[Ps 76:10|Or will God forget to shew mercy? or will he in his anger shut up his mercies?|Aut obliviscetur misereri Deus, aut continebit in ira sua misericordias suas?]]

paras.t: Ad te, Domine, faciem meam converto, ad te oculos meos erigo. Certum est, quod ad illocalem et incircumscriptibilem supersimplicissimum Deum Sara converterit faciem suam interiorem, videlicet mentem: de qua in Psalmo, Tibi dixit cor meum, exquisivit te facies mea. Sic et oculos interiores erexit ad Deum altissimum ubique præsentem, juxta illud: Oculi mei semper ad Dominum. Exteriorem quoque faciem et oculos corporales levavit et direxit ad Deum, id est ad locum in quo Deus specialiter esse et habitare asseritur, puta ad cœlum, vel pro tunc ad templum versus Jerusalem: secundum quod in Daniele legitur, Danielem in suo cœnaculo apertis fenestris orasse contra Jerusalem. Sic etenim Judæi in captivitate positi solebant orare, prout libro tertio Regum Salomon dixit: Si in terra inimicorum ad quam captivi ducti fuerint, oraverint te, contra viam terræ suæ et templi quod ædificavi, exaudies eos.
paras.en: [[3:14|To thee, O Lord, I turn my face|Ad te, Domine, faciem meam converto]], [[3:14|to thee I direct my eyes|ad te oculos meos erigo]] [Denis reads *erigo*, "I lift up", where the Vulgate has *dirigo*, "I direct"]. It is certain that Sara turned her inner face, namely her mind, to God, who is in no place, who cannot be circumscribed, and who is simple above all simplicity: of which face it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 26:8|My heart hath said to thee: My face hath sought thee|Tibi dixit cor meum, exquisivit te facies mea]]. So too she lifted up her inner eyes to the most high God, who is present everywhere, according to that: [[Ps 24:15|My eyes are ever towards the Lord|Oculi mei semper ad Dominum]]. Her outward face also and her bodily eyes she raised and directed to God, that is, to the place in which God is said especially to be and to dwell, namely to heaven, or, for that time, to the temple, towards Jerusalem: as we read in Daniel that Daniel prayed in his upper chamber with the windows open towards Jerusalem[[Dan 6:10||]]. For so the Jews set in captivity were wont to pray, as Solomon said in the third book of Kings: If [[3 Kings 8:48|in the land of their enemies, to which they have been led captives|in terra inimicorum ad quam captivi ducti fuerint]], they [[3 Kings 8:48|pray to thee towards the way of their land|oraverint te, contra viam terræ suæ]] [[3 Kings 8:48|and of the temple which I have built|et templi quod ædificavi]], then [[3 Kings 8:49|hear thou|exaudies eos]] them.

paras.t: Peto, Domine, ut de vinculo improperii hujus absolvas me, id est de dura et falsa ista diffamia, qua velut catenis circumdata sum: quod virgini tenerrimæ fuit gravissimum, quum virgines præsertim castæ et piæ, sint maxime verecundæ; aut certe de super terram eripias me, id est, in pace tollas spiritum meum a corpore isto mortali. Hoc oravit eo modo, quo expositum est de Tobia, et ne alii tam enormiter scandalizarentur in ea, et ne ipsa per impatientiam laberetur. Sic quippe electi interdum de vita hac tolluntur celerius, juxta illud Sapientis: Vivens inter peccatores, translatus est. Raptus est, ne malitia mutaret intellectum illius, aut ne fictio deciperet animam ejus.
paras.en: [[3:15|I beg, O Lord, that thou loose me from the bond of this reproach|Peto, Domine, ut de vinculo improperii hujus absolvas me]], that is, from this harsh and false defamation, with which I am bound about as with chains: which was most grievous to a most tender virgin, since virgins, above all chaste and devout ones, are exceedingly modest; [[3:15|or else take me away from the earth|aut certe de super terram eripias me]], that is, take my spirit in peace from this mortal body. She prayed this in the manner explained of Tobias, and so that others should not be so grievously scandalized in her, and that she herself should not fall through impatience. For so the elect are sometimes taken the sooner from this life, according to that of the Wise man: [[Wis 4:10|living among sinners, he was translated|Vivens inter peccatores, translatus est]]. [[Wis 4:11|He was taken away, lest wickedness should alter his understanding, or deceit beguile his soul.|Raptus est, ne malitia mutaret intellectum illius, aut ne fictio deciperet animam ejus]]

paras.t: Tu scis, Domine, quia nunquam concupivi virum, voluptatis amore, sed desiderio prolis ad Dei obsequium educandæ: ut paulo post subditur; et mundam servavi animam meam, auxilio gratiæ tuæ, ab omni concupiscentia sensuali inordinata venereorum, imo et aliorum sensibilium objectorum: quod fuit in tali puella grandis perfectio. Quæ ad Dei honorem, non jactanter, hic profitetur, ad augendum sibi ipsi in Deo fiduciam in tanta angustia, sicut et Ezechias rex angustiis circumdatus, dixit: Memento, Domine, quomodo ambulaverim coram te in veritate et corde perfecto.
paras.en: [[3:16|Thou knowest, O Lord, that I never coveted a husband|Tu scis, Domine, quia nunquam concupivi virum]] out of love of pleasure, but from desire of offspring to be brought up for the service of God, as is added a little after; [[3:16|and have kept my soul clean|et mundam servavi animam meam]], by the help of thy grace, [[3:16|from all lust|ab omni concupiscentia]], that is, from all inordinate sensual desire of venereal things, nay and of other objects of sense as well [*concupiscentia*, "lust" in the verse, is any desire of the senses, so Denis extends it]: which was a great perfection in such a maiden. These things she professes here to the honour of God, not boastfully, to increase her own confidence in God in so great a strait, just as King Ezechias too, beset by straits, said: [[4 Kings 20:3|O Lord, remember how I have walked before thee in truth, and with a perfect heart|Memento, Domine, quomodo ambulaverim coram te in veritate et corde perfecto]] [the same words stand at Is 38:3].

paras.t: Nunquam cum ludentibus miscui me, hoc est, in ludicris et humanis solatiis nunquam excessi, vel ea omnino vitavi: in quibus tamen potest se homo virtuose habere per virtutem moralem, quæ eutrapelia vocatur. Sic et Jeremias, Non sedi (inquit) in concilio ludentium. Interdum vero ludus in malo accipitur pro actu dissoluto; quandoque vero in bono, secundum illud Regum: David percutiebat in organis et ludebat totis viribus coram Domino. Neque cum his qui in levitate ambulant participem me præbui; id est, choreas, spectacula, et quidquid maturitati morum contrariatur, ac vana consortia evitavi. Et sic Sara ista cum Esther dicere potuit Deo: Nunquam lætata est ancilla tua, nisi in te, Deus Israel.
paras.en: [[3:17|Never have I joined myself with them that play|Nunquam cum ludentibus miscui me]], that is, I have never gone to excess in games and human recreations, or I have shunned them altogether: in which, however, a man can behave virtuously through the moral virtue called eutrapelia [that is, the virtue of right measure in jest and play]. So too Jeremias: [[Jer 15:17|I sat not|Non sedi]] (he says) [[Jer 15:17|in the assembly of jesters|in concilio ludentium]] [*ludentium*, "jesters" here, is the word rendered "them that play" in the verse]. Now play is sometimes taken in a bad sense, for a dissolute act; but sometimes in a good one, according to that of Kings: David struck upon instruments and played with all his might before the Lord[[2 Kings 6:5||]][[1 Par 13:8||]] [Denis joins 2 Kings 6:5, "David and all Israel played before the Lord", with 6:14, "David danced with all his might"; the margin gives II Kings vi and 1 Par. xiii, 8]. [[3:17|neither have I made myself partaker with them that walk in lightness|Neque cum his qui in levitate ambulant participem me præbui]]; that is, I have shunned dances, shows, and whatever is contrary to seriousness of manners, and vain company. And so this Sara could say to God with Esther: [[Esth 14:18|thy handmaid hath never rejoiced|Nunquam lætata est ancilla tua]], [[Esth 14:18|but in thee|nisi in te]], O God of Israel.

paras.t: Virum autem, hoc est viros cum quibus contraxi, cum timore tuo filiali, non cum libidine mea, consensi accipere, juxta meorum voluntatem parentum. Ad matrimonium namque requiritur consensus animorum. Et congrue ait, Cum timore tuo. Quamvis enim actus carnalis conjugii possit sine peccato exerceri, raro tamen contingit sine alicujus culpæ admixtione. Multa quoque sunt matrimonii onera. Propter quod de conjugatis ait Apostolus: Tribulationem carnis habebunt hujusmodi. Sed et mulier ponitur sub potestate mariti: ideo sapiens virgo non sine grandi timore consensit in virum.
paras.en: [[3:18|But a husband|Virum autem]], that is, the husbands with whom I contracted marriage, [[3:18|with thy fear|cum timore tuo]], filial fear [the fear of a child who dreads to offend, as opposed to servile fear, which dreads punishment], [[3:18|not with my lust|non cum libidine mea]], [[3:18|I consented to take|consensi accipere]], according to the will of my parents. For the consent of minds is required for marriage. And fittingly she says, [[3:18|with thy fear|Cum timore tuo]]. For although the carnal act of marriage can be exercised without sin, yet it rarely happens without the admixture of some fault. The burdens of marriage too are many. Hence the Apostle says of the married: [[1 Cor 7:28|such shall have tribulation of the flesh|Tribulationem carnis habebunt hujusmodi]]. And the woman, moreover, is put under the power of her husband: so the wise virgin did not consent to a husband without great fear.

paras.t: Et, aut ego indigna fui illis. Hoc dicit ex humilitate, ne videatur se incaute illis præferre. Et quamvis jam suas commemoravit virtuositates, finaliter tamen se commisit divino judicio, sciens quod homo frequenter habeat quasdam culpas occultas, de quibus sibi conscius non est. Unde Apostolus dixit: Nihil mihi conscius sum, sed non in hoc justificatus sum. Qui autem judicat me, Dominus est. Et Psalmista oravit: Ab occultis meis munda me, Domine. Aut illi forsitan me non fuerunt digni: quasi dicat, De hoc nil temere audeo judicare. Quia forsitan viro alii conservasti me. Hoc ex divina inspiratione pro sua consolatione aliqualiter intellexit. Deus enim interdum revelat homini aliquid perfecte, aliquando imperfecte, secundum moderamen sapientiæ suæ.
paras.en: [[3:19|And either I was unworthy of them|Et, aut ego indigna fui illis]]. She says this out of humility, lest she seem rashly to prefer herself to them. And although she had already recounted her virtues, yet in the end she committed herself to the divine judgement, knowing that a man often has certain hidden faults of which he is not conscious. Whence the Apostle said: [[1 Cor 4:4|I am not conscious to myself of anything. Yet am I not hereby justified: but he that judgeth me is the Lord|Nihil mihi conscius sum, sed non in hoc justificatus sum. Qui autem judicat me, Dominus est]]. And the Psalmist prayed: [[Ps 18:13|from my secret ones cleanse me, O Lord|Ab occultis meis munda me, Domine]]. [[3:19|or they perhaps were not worthy of me|Aut illi forsitan me non fuerunt digni]]: as if she said, Of this I dare judge nothing rashly. [[3:19|because perhaps thou hast kept me for another man|Quia forsitan viro alii conservasti me]]. This she understood in some measure by divine inspiration, for her comfort. For God sometimes reveals something to a man perfectly, sometimes imperfectly, according to the measure of his wisdom.

paras.t: Non est enim in hominis potestate consilium tuum, hoc est dispositio providentiæ tuæ, seu ordinatio tui propositi ac decreti, quod invariabile est, nec potestati subjacet creaturæ. Ideo in Isaia testatur: Consilium meum stabit, et omnis voluntas mea fiet. Verumtamen consilium proprie sumptum, prout est inquisitio de agendis, non convenit Deo. Sic enim est ignorantis naturæ, ut asserit Damascenus, ut frequenter dictum est alibi.
paras.en: [[3:20|For thy counsel is not in man's power|Non est enim in hominis potestate consilium tuum]], that is, the disposition of thy providence, or the ordinance of thy purpose and decree, which is unchangeable, and is not subject to the power of any creature. Therefore he testifies in Isaias: [[Is 46:10|My counsel shall stand, and all my will shall be done|Consilium meum stabit, et omnis voluntas mea fiet]]. Yet counsel taken properly, as an inquiry into what is to be done, does not befit God [*consilium* means both a design and the deliberation that leads to it]. For so taken it belongs to a nature that does not know, as Damascene asserts, and as has often been said elsewhere.

paras.t: Hoc autem pro certo habet omnis qui colit te, certitudine adhærentiæ, quæ est fidei certitudo: certitudo autem evidentiæ, est scientiæ certitudo; quod vita ejus si in probatione fuerit, hoc est in examinatione et exercitatione adversitatum, coronabitur a te corona æternæ felicitatis: dummodo constans atque fidelis manserit in adversis, quum scriptum sit: Tanquam aurum in fornace, probavit electos Dominus, et quasi holocausti hostiam accepit eos. Ideo accipient regnum decoris, et diadema speciei de manu Domini. Hinc sanctus Job: Probavit me (inquit) quasi aurum quod per ignem transit. Atque Apostolus: Non coronatur, nisi qui legitime certaverit.
paras.en: [[3:21|But this every one is sure of that worshippeth thee|Hoc autem pro certo habet omnis qui colit te]], with the certainty of adherence, which is the certainty of faith [that is, the firmness with which the mind clings to what it believes, as against the certainty of evidence, which comes from seeing the thing itself]; whereas the certainty of evidence is the certainty of knowledge; [[3:21|that his life, if it be under trial|quod vita ejus si in probatione fuerit]], that is, in the testing and exercise of adversities, [[3:21|shall be crowned|coronabitur]] by thee with the crown of eternal happiness: provided he remain constant and faithful in adversity, since it is written: [[Wis 3:6|As gold in the furnace, he hath proved them, and as a victim of a holocaust, he hath received them|Tanquam aurum in fornace, probavit electos Dominus, et quasi holocausti hostiam accepit eos]] [Denis reads "the Lord hath proved the elect" where the verse has "he hath proved them"]. [[Wis 5:17|Therefore shall they receive a kingdom of glory, and a crown of beauty at the hand of the Lord|Ideo accipient regnum decoris, et diadema speciei de manu Domini]]. Hence holy Job: [[Job 23:10|has tried me|Probavit me]] (he says) [[Job 23:10|as gold that passeth through the fire|quasi aurum quod per ignem transit]]. And the Apostle: [[2 Tim 2:5|is not crowned, except he strive lawfully|Non coronatur, nisi qui legitime certaverit]].

paras.t: Si autem in tribulatione fuerit, liberabitur: dummodo tribulationem pro suis peccatis et intuitu Dei æquanimiter tulerit, dicens illud Michææ: Iram Domini portabo, quia peccavi ei. Si vero fuerit in tribulatione interna, quæ est ipsa contritio de peccatis, misericordiam consequetur. Hinc scriptum est: Non consurget duplex tribulatio. Nihilo minus multi de tribulatione sæculi hujus ad tribulationem corruunt infernalem, quia in tribulatione non pœnitent.
paras.en: [[3:21|and if it be under tribulation, it shall be delivered|Si autem in tribulatione fuerit, liberabitur]]: provided he bear the tribulation with an even mind, for his sins and with his eyes on God, saying that of Micheas: [[Mich 7:9|I will bear the wrath of the Lord, because I have sinned against him|Iram Domini portabo, quia peccavi ei]]. But if he is in inward tribulation, which is contrition itself for sins, he will obtain mercy. Hence it is written: [[Nah 1:9|there shall not rise a double affliction|Non consurget duplex tribulatio]] [*tribulatio*, "affliction" in this verse, is the word of Tobias 3:21]. None the less many fall from the tribulation of this world into the tribulation of hell, because in tribulation they do not repent.

paras.t: Et si in correptione fuerit, hoc est in castigatione seu reprehensione pro suis peccatis, ad misericordiam pervenire licebit, quando ipsam correptionem capit gratanter. Ideo scriptum est in Job: Beatus homo qui corripitur a Domino. Increpationem ergo Domini ne reprobes. Nam et Dominus fassus est in Apocalypsi: Ego, quos amo, arguo et castigo.
paras.en: [[3:21|and if it be under correction|Et si in correptione fuerit]], that is, in chastisement or reproof for his sins, [[3:21|it shall be allowed to come to thy mercy|ad misericordiam pervenire licebit]], when he takes the correction itself gladly. Therefore it is written in Job: [[Job 5:17|Blessed is the man whom God correcteth: refuse not, therefore, the chastising of the Lord|Beatus homo qui corripitur a Domino. Increpationem ergo Domini ne reprobes]]. For the Lord too declared in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 3:19|Such as I love, I rebuke and chastise|Ego, quos amo, arguo et castigo]].

paras.t: Non enim delectaris in perditionibus nostris, hoc est condemnatione et punitione nostra, secundum quod sunt pœnæ atque miseriæ quædam, juxta illud Sapientis: Deus mortem non fecit, nec lætatur in perditione vivorum. Delectatur autem in nostra emendatione et salvatione. Propter quod in Ezechiele locutus est: Numquid voluntatis meæ est mors impii, et non ut convertatur et vivat? Nihilo minus in punitionibus et condemnationibus impiorum, secundum quod sunt effectus divinæ justitiæ, delectatur, sicut et justi, qui lætabuntur quum viderint vindictam. Propter quod in Proverbiis disseruit: Ego in interitu vestro ridebo. Et in Isaia: Ego consolabor super hostibus meis. Hinc loquitur per Osee: Juxta desiderium meum corripiam eos.
paras.en: [[3:22|For thou art not delighted in our being lost|Non enim delectaris in perditionibus nostris]], that is, in our condemnation and punishment, in so far as these are pains and miseries, according to that of the Wise man: [[Wis 1:13|God made not death, neither hath he pleasure in the destruction of the living|Deus mortem non fecit, nec lætatur in perditione vivorum]]. But he delights in our amendment and salvation. Hence he spoke in Ezechiel: [[Ezech 18:23|Is it my will that a sinner should die|Numquid voluntatis meæ est mors impii]], [[Ezech 18:23|and not that he should be converted|et non ut convertatur]], [[Ezech 18:23|and live?|et vivat?]] None the less he does delight in the punishments and condemnations of the wicked, in so far as they are effects of the divine justice, as do the just also, who shall rejoice when they see vengeance[[Ps 57:11||]]. Hence he declared in Proverbs: [[Prov 1:26|I also will laugh in your destruction|Ego in interitu vestro ridebo]]. And in Isaias: [[Is 1:24|I will comfort myself over my adversaries|Ego consolabor super hostibus meis]]. Hence he speaks by Osee: [[Osee 10:10|According to my desire, I will chastise them|Juxta desiderium meum corripiam eos]].

paras.t: Quia post tempestatem tranquillum facis, hoc est, post afflictionem, tentationem, et contritionis dolorem, confers pectoris pacem seu tranquillitatem internam; et post lacrimationem et fletum ex piis et rationabilibus causis, exsultationem infundis, id est consolationem internam in isto exsilio, deinde æternam jucunditatem in regno. Hoc est quod in Matthæo ait: Beati qui lugent, quoniam ipsi consolabuntur. Et in Psalmo: Transivimus per ignem et aquam, et eduxisti nos in refrigerium. De quo fertur in Job: Ipse vulnerat, et medetur; percutit, et manus ejus sanabunt.
paras.en: [[3:22|because after a storm thou makest a calm|Quia post tempestatem tranquillum facis]], that is, after affliction, temptation, and the pain of contrition, thou bestowest peace of heart, or inward tranquillity; [[3:22|and after tears and weeping|et post lacrimationem et fletum]] shed for holy and reasonable causes, [[3:22|thou pourest in joyfulness|exsultationem infundis]], that is, inward consolation in this exile, and afterwards everlasting gladness in the kingdom. This is what he says in Matthew: [[Matt 5:5|Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.|Beati qui lugent, quoniam ipsi consolabuntur]] And in the Psalm: [[Ps 65:12|We have passed through fire and water, and thou hast brought us out into a refreshment|Transivimus per ignem et aquam, et eduxisti nos in refrigerium]]. Of whom it is said in Job: [[Job 5:18|he woundeth, and cureth: he striketh, and his hands shall heal|Ipse vulnerat, et medetur; percutit, et manus ejus sanabunt]] [the margin gives Job x, 15; the words are Job 5:18].

paras.t: Sit nomen tuum, Deus Israel, benedictum in sæcula, hoc est æternaliter.
paras.en: [[3:23|Be thy name, O God of Israel, blessed for ever|Sit nomen tuum, Deus Israel, benedictum in sæcula]], that is, eternally.

paras.t: In illo tempore exauditæ sunt preces amborum, videlicet Tobiæ et Saræ, non quoad hoc quod petierunt tolli de vita hac, sed quoad hoc quod relevamen a suis tribulationibus petierunt; in conspectu gloriæ summi Dei, hoc est a Deo majestatis immensæ.
paras.en: [[3:24|At that time the prayers of them both were heard|In illo tempore exauditæ sunt preces amborum]], namely of Tobias and Sara, not as to their asking to be taken from this life, but as to their asking for relief from their tribulations; [[3:24|in the sight of the glory of the most high God|in conspectu gloriæ summi Dei]], that is, by the God of boundless majesty.

paras.t: Et missus est angelus Domini sanctus Raphael: qui interpretatur, medicina Dei, quia per ipsum Deus curavit hos ambos. Unde subjungitur: ut curaret eos ambos, hoc est Tobiam a cæcitate et mentis afflictione, Saram quoque a vinculo improperii sui et sterilitatis opprobrio atque diffamia; quorum uno tempore sunt orationes in conspectu Domini recitatæ, id est Deo oblatæ per angelos sanctos illorum duorum custodes: non quod Deum aliquid lateat, sed quia angeli sancti precibus hominum impendunt suffragia, et orant pro sibi commissis, atque imperfectum eorum pie excusant. Sic et in Actibus angelus sanctus legitur dixisse Cornelio: Orationes tuæ et eleemosynæ tuæ ascenderunt in memoriam in conspectu Dei. Itemque: Eleemosynæ tuæ commemoratæ sunt in conspectu Dei.
paras.en: [[3:25|And the holy angel of the Lord, Raphael was sent|Et missus est angelus Domini sanctus Raphael]]: which is interpreted "medicine of God", since through him God healed these two. Hence there is added: [[3:25|to heal them both|ut curaret eos ambos]], that is, Tobias of his blindness and his affliction of mind, and Sara of the bond of her reproach, and of the shame and ill repute of barrenness; [[3:25|whose prayers at one time were rehearsed in the sight of the Lord|quorum uno tempore sunt orationes in conspectu Domini recitatæ]], that is, offered to God by the holy angels who were the guardians of those two: not that anything is hidden from God, but because the holy angels lend their support to men's prayers, and pray for those committed to them, and kindly excuse their imperfection. So too in the Acts the holy angel is read to have said to Cornelius: [[Acts 10:4|Thy prayers and thy alms are ascended for a memorial in the sight of God|Orationes tuæ et eleemosynæ tuæ ascenderunt in memoriam in conspectu Dei]]. And again: [[Acts 10:31|thy alms are had in remembrance in the sight of God|Eleemosynæ tuæ commemoratæ sunt in conspectu Dei]].

paras.t: Ex præhabitis edocemur, in omni tribulatione atque angustia ad Deum per orationes ferventes confugere, pro parentibus tam vivis quam mortuis specialiter exorare, increpationes etiam ab inferioribus, et criminationes falsas patienter sufferre, nec contra increpantes contendere, Deum quoque benedicere in suis judiciis, et omnem excessum vitare in levitatibus, ludis, jocis ac risibus, atque in desolationibus consolationem divinam æquanimiter præstolari.
paras.en: From what has been said we are taught to flee to God by fervent prayers in every tribulation and strait; to pray especially for our parents, both living and dead; to bear patiently rebukes even from inferiors, and false accusations, and not to quarrel with those who rebuke us; to bless God also in his judgements; to avoid all excess in levities, games, jests and laughter; and in desolations to await the divine consolation with an even mind.

4.title: Elucidatio capituli quarti: Igitur quum Tobias putaret orationem suam exaudiri
4.title_en: Explanation of the fourth chapter: Therefore when Tobias thought that his prayer was heard

paras.t: Recitantur hic moralissima ac saluberrima documenta, quibus senior Tobias filium suum, et per eum universos instruxit fideles. Igitur quum Tobias putaret orationem suam exaudiri a Deo, ut mori potuisset, hoc est quoad hoc, quod cito (prout petiit) moreretur. Qualiter autem fuerit ejus oratio exaudita, patuit in præcedentis expositione capituli. Vocavit ad se Tobiam filium suum, dixitque ei: Audi, fili mi, verba oris mei, et ea in corde tuo quasi fundamentum construe, hoc est, firmissime ea imprime tuæ memoriæ. Consueverunt autem sancti patres, emigraturi de sæculo isto, sobolem suam salubriter exhortari, benedicere, informare, ut patet in Genesi de Jacob, et primo Paralipomenon de David. Sic et Christus post cœnam novissimam, passione sua instante, suos discipulos copiosissime informavit.
paras.en: Here are set out most moral and wholesome teachings, with which the elder Tobias instructed his son, and through him all the faithful. [[4:1|Therefore when Tobias thought that his prayer was heard|Igitur quum Tobias putaret orationem suam exaudiri]] by God [[4:1|that he might die|ut mori potuisset]]: that is, as regards this, that he should die soon (as he had asked). How his prayer was heard was shown in the explanation of the preceding chapter[[Tob 3:24||]] [the margin here is hard to read, apparently citing Tob. iii]. [[4:1|he called to him Tobias his son|Vocavit ad se Tobiam filium suum]], [[4:2|And said to him|dixitque ei]]: [[4:2|Hear, my son, the words of my mouth, and lay them as a foundation in thy heart|Audi, fili mi, verba oris mei, et ea in corde tuo quasi fundamentum construe]], that is, impress them most firmly on thy memory. Now the holy fathers, when about to depart from this world, were wont to exhort their offspring for their salvation, to bless them and instruct them, as is plain in Genesis of Jacob[[Gen 49:1||]], and in the first book of Paralipomenon of David[[1 Par 28:1||]]. So too Christ, after the last supper, with his passion at hand, instructed his disciples most fully[[John 13:1||]] [the margin gives John xiii–xvii].

paras.t: Quum acceperit Deus animam meam, separando eam a corpore, et in sinu Abrahæ eam ponendo, eamque (ut spero) misericorditer amplectendo, corpus meum sepeli, secundum quod ego sollicitus fui aliorum exstincta corpora sepelire, sciens quod in die resurgent novissimo. Sicque committimus ea terræ tanquam deposita quædam quæ suo tempore resumemus. Et honorem habebis, id est exhibebis, matri tuæ omnibus diebus vitæ ejus. Proles namque tenetur parentibus obedientiam et reverentiam, atque si indiguerint, necessariorum procurationem: a quibus beneficia tanta suscepit. Hinc subditur: Memor enim debes esse, quæ et quanta pericula passa sit propter te in utero suo: præsertim in partu, quo dolor, tremor, mœror, pressura, angustia, occupant et adimplent parturientem.
paras.en: [[4:3|When God shall take my soul|Quum acceperit Deus animam meam]], by separating it from the body, and placing it in the bosom of Abraham[[Luke 16:23||]], and (as I hope) mercifully embracing it, [[4:3|thou shalt bury my body|corpus meum sepeli]], even as I was careful to bury the lifeless bodies of others, knowing that they will rise again on the last day. And so we commit them to the earth as deposits which we shall take up again in their time. [[4:3|and thou shalt honour|Et honorem habebis]], that is, show honour to, [[4:3|thy mother all the days of her life|matri tuæ omnibus diebus vitæ ejus]]. For offspring is bound to give its parents obedience and reverence, and, if they are in need, to provide them with necessaries, since it has received such great benefits from them. Hence it is added: [[4:4|For thou must be mindful what and how great perils she suffered for thee in her womb|Memor enim debes esse, quæ et quanta pericula passa sit propter te in utero suo]]: above all in childbirth, when pain, trembling, grief, distress and anguish seize and fill the woman in labour.

paras.t: Quum autem et ipsa compleverit tempus vitæ suæ, sepelias eam circa me: ut quorum unus fuit lectus, unus sit tumulus, atque ut simul salubriter resurgamus, et qui conjuncti eramus in vita, non separemur post mortem. In his innotescunt patientia atque justitia venerandi Tobiæ, qui non obstante quod tam acriter et injuste fuit derisus a conjuge, ut patuit, tam diligenter commisit filio suo de cura illius.
paras.en: [[4:5|And when she also shall have ended the time of her life|Quum autem et ipsa compleverit tempus vitæ suæ]], [[4:5|bury her by me|sepelias eam circa me]]: so that those who had one bed may have one tomb, and that we may rise again together unto salvation, and we who were joined in life may not be parted after death. In these words the patience and justice of the venerable Tobias come to light: although he had been so bitterly and unjustly derided by his wife, as was shown[[Tob 2:22||]], he so carefully charged his son with her care.

paras.t: Omnibus autem diebus vitæ tuæ in mente habeto Deum, ad minus per habitum fidei, spei et caritatis, et quantum fieri potest per actus earumdem ac aliarum virtutum, pensando jugiter præsentiam Dei, implendoque illud Psalmographi, Meditatio cordis mei in conspectu tuo semper; et, Oculi mei semper ad Dominum. Et cave ne aliquando peccato consentias. Hoc est quod ait Apostolus: Nolite locum dare diabolo. Et prætermittas præcepta Dei, id est, cave ne negligas ea implere. Ideo in Ecclesiastico habetur: Salutare sacrificium est, attendere mandatis, et discedere ab omni iniquitate. A qua qualiter sit discedendum, tangitur in eodem, quum dicitur: Quasi a facie colubri fuge peccata.
paras.en: [[4:6|And all the days of thy life have God in thy mind|Omnibus autem diebus vitæ tuæ in mente habeto Deum]], at least by the habit of faith, hope and charity, and as far as can be, by the acts of these and of the other virtues, constantly weighing the presence of God, and fulfilling that word of the Psalmist, [[Ps 18:15|the meditation of my heart always in thy sight|Meditatio cordis mei in conspectu tuo semper]]; and, [[Ps 24:15|My eyes are ever towards the Lord|Oculi mei semper ad Dominum]]. [[4:6|and take heed thou never consent to sin|Et cave ne aliquando peccato consentias]]. This is what the Apostle says: [[Eph 4:27|Give not place to the devil|Nolite locum dare diabolo]]. [[4:6|nor transgress the commandments of the Lord|Et prætermittas præcepta Dei]], that is, take care not to neglect to fulfil them. Therefore it is said in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 35:2|It is a wholesome sacrifice to take heed to the commandments, and to depart from all iniquity|Salutare sacrificium est, attendere mandatis, et discedere ab omni iniquitate]]. How one must depart from it is touched on in the same book, where it is said: [[Ecclus 21:2|Flee from sins as from the face of a serpent|Quasi a facie colubri fuge peccata]].

paras.t: Insuper, quo Tobias actibus misericordiæ excellentius fuit intentus, eo ad ipsos efficacius ferventiusque hortatur, addendo: Ex substantia tua fac eleemosynam, et noli avertere faciem tuam ab ullo paupere te rogante, quin ad minus pie adspicias eum, ut consoleris verbo aut signo, si non habes corporale subsidium quod impendas. Ita enim fiet, ut nec a te avertatur facies Domini, id est divinæ pietatis respectus. Beati enim misericordes, quoniam ipsi misericordiam consequentur. Et quanto quis proximis fuerit propter Deum benignior, eo Omnipotens gratiosior erit ei. Quomodo potueris, ita esto misericors, hoc est compassivus atque subveniens: sicut consequenter exponitur. Si multum tibi fuerit, abundanter tribue unicuique partem; si exiguum tibi fuerit, etiam exiguum libenter impertiri stude cum liberali affectu. Deus etenim magis pensat affectum, quam donum; et magis perpendit ex quanto, quam quantum. Ideo de paupercula mittente in gazophylacium duo minuta, dixit Salvator: Quia hæc vidua plus omnibus misit.
paras.en: Moreover, the more excellently Tobias was intent on works of mercy, the more effectively and fervently he exhorts to them, adding: [[4:7|Give alms out of thy substance|Ex substantia tua fac eleemosynam]], [[4:7|and turn not away thy face from any poor person|et noli avertere faciem tuam ab ullo paupere]] who asks of thee, but at least look kindly on him, so as to comfort him by word or sign, if thou hast no bodily help to bestow. [[4:7|for so it shall come to pass that the face of the Lord shall not be turned from thee|Ita enim fiet, ut nec a te avertatur facies Domini]], that is, the regard of the divine mercy. [[Matt 5:7|Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy|Beati enim misericordes, quoniam ipsi misericordiam consequentur]]. And the kinder anyone is to his neighbours for God's sake, the more gracious the Almighty will be to him. [[4:8|According to thy ability be merciful|Quomodo potueris, ita esto misericors]], that is, compassionate and helping, as is set out next. [[4:9|If thou have much give abundantly|Si multum tibi fuerit, abundanter tribue]] to each a share; [[4:9|if thou have little, take care even so to bestow willingly a little|si exiguum tibi fuerit, etiam exiguum libenter impertiri stude]] with a generous heart. For God weighs the affection more than the gift, and considers more from how much than how much [that is, how much the giver had to give from, rather than the size of the gift]. Therefore of the poor widow casting two mites into the treasury, the Saviour said: [[Mark 12:43|this poor widow hath cast in more than all|hæc vidua plus omnibus misit]].

paras.t: Præmium enim bonum tibi thesaurisas, hoc est, acquiris et reponis: quod invenies in die necessitatis, id est mortis et judicii tui particularis ac universalis, et item in purgatorii pœnis, in quibus vivorum suffragia tantum prosunt, quantum defuncti hic meruerunt ut eis prodesse possint, hoc est, quo misericordiores fuerint. Hinc teste Ambrosio, Summa christianæ religionis in caritate et pietate consistit. Augustinus quoque asserit: Sola misericordia comes est defunctorum. Unde testatur Psalmista: Beatus qui intelligit super egenum et pauperem; in die mala liberabit eum Dominus.
paras.en: [[4:10|For thus thou storest up to thyself a good reward|Præmium enim bonum tibi thesaurisas]], that is, thou gainest and layest up, which thou wilt find [[4:10|for the day of necessity|in die necessitatis]]: that is, of death and of thy judgement, particular and universal, and likewise in the pains of purgatory, in which the suffrages of the living avail as much as the departed deserved here that they should avail them, that is, the more merciful they were. Hence, as Ambrose witnesses, the sum of the Christian religion consists in charity and loving-kindness. Augustine also asserts: Mercy alone is the companion of the dead. Whence the Psalmist testifies: [[Ps 40:2|Blessed is he that understandeth concerning the needy and the poor: the Lord will deliver him in the evil day|Beatus qui intelligit super egenum et pauperem; in die mala liberabit eum Dominus]].

paras.t: Quoniam eleemosyna ab omni peccato et a morte infernalis miseriæ liberat, dummodo fiat ex caritate et virtute misericordiæ; et non patietur animam ire in tenebras Acherontis. Et dato quod fiat extra caritatem, frequenter tamen de congruo gratiam promeretur, et intercessione ac meritis eorum quibus impenditur, gratia conversionis frequenter eleemosynariis datur. Hinc in Evangelio Dominus loquitur: Quod superest, date eleemosynam, et ecce omnia munda sunt vobis. Itemque: Facite vobis amicos de mammona iniquitatis, ut quum defeceritis, recipiant vos in æterna tabernacula. Fiducia magna, hoc est causa magnæ fiduciæ, erit coram summo Deo eleemosyna tam corporalis quam spiritualis, omnibus facientibus eam. De operibus quippe misericordiæ perhibet Christus se disceptaturum in die judicii, misericordibusque dicturum: Venite, benedicti Patris mei, percipite regnum.
paras.en: [[4:11|For alms deliver from all sin, and from death|Quoniam eleemosyna ab omni peccato et a morte]] of hellish misery, provided it be done out of charity and the virtue of mercy; [[4:11|and will not suffer the soul to go into darkness|et non patietur animam ire in tenebras]] of Acheron. And granted that it be done outside charity, yet it often merits grace de congruo [that is, by a certain fittingness, not as a strict due], and through the intercession and merits of those on whom it is bestowed, the grace of conversion is often given to almsgivers. Hence the Lord says in the Gospel: [[Luke 11:41|that which remaineth, give alms: and behold, all things are clean unto you|Quod superest, date eleemosynam, et ecce omnia munda sunt vobis]]. And again: [[Luke 16:9|Make unto you friends of the mammon of iniquity: that when you shall fail, they may receive you into everlasting dwellings|Facite vobis amicos de mammona iniquitatis, ut quum defeceritis, recipiant vos in æterna tabernacula]]. [[4:12|Alms shall be a great confidence|Fiducia magna]], that is, a cause of great confidence, [[4:12|before the most high God|erit coram summo Deo]], alms both bodily and spiritual, [[4:12|to all them that give it|omnibus facientibus eam]]. For Christ declares that on the day of judgement he will judge by the works of mercy, and will say to the merciful: [[Matt 25:34|Come, ye blessed of my Father|Venite, benedicti Patris mei]], [[Matt 25:34|possess you the kingdom|percipite regnum]].

paras.t: Attende tibi ab omni fornicatione, tam simplici, quam adulterio, incestu, stupro, sacrilegio; a spirituali etiam fornicatione, præsertim ab idololatria. Et præter uxorem tuam, quam habiturus es, nunquam patiaris crimen scire, hoc est, nunquam alteri commiscearis, nec conscius tibi fias criminis tanti.
paras.en: [[4:13|Take heed to keep thyself, my son, from all fornication|Attende tibi ab omni fornicatione]], simple fornication as well as adultery[[Matt 5:27||]], incest, seduction, sacrilege; and from spiritual fornication too, above all from idolatry. [[4:13|and beside thy wife|Et præter uxorem tuam]], whom thou art to have, [[4:13|never endure to know a crime|nunquam patiaris crimen scire]], that is, never have intercourse with another, nor make thyself privy to so great a crime.

paras.t: Superbiam nunquam in tuo sensu interiori aut exteriori, aut in tuo verbo, imo nec facto, neque vestitu, nec aliquo apparatu, dominari permittas, ei consentiendo. Idcirco, si subrepat, mox reprime eam, et abjice tanquam diabolicum crimen, maledictionisque semen, et venenum mortiferum ac vitiorum originem, matrem, reginam. In ipsa enim initium sumpsit omnis perditio: quia per superbiam primus ille apostata angelus perdidit semetipsum, et angelos innumerabiles sibi attraxit; atque ex illa perditione consecuta et orta est invidia diaboli, per quam mors intravit in orbem terrarum, ut Sapiens disserit.
paras.en: [[4:14|Never suffer pride to reign in thy mind|Superbiam nunquam in tuo sensu]], inward or outward, [[4:14|or in thy words|aut in tuo verbo]], nay, nor in deed, nor in dress, nor in any display, by consenting to it. Therefore, if it creeps in, repress it at once, and cast it away as a devilish crime, the seed of malediction, a deadly poison, and the origin, mother and queen of the vices. [[4:14|for from it all perdition took its beginning|In ipsa enim initium sumpsit omnis perditio]]: because through pride that first apostate angel lost himself[[Is 14:4||]] [the margin gives Is. xiv, 4 and following; the fall of Lucifer is at Is 14:12], and drew innumerable angels after him; and from that perdition there followed and arose the envy of the devil, through which [[Wis 2:24|death came into the world|mors intravit in orbem terrarum]], as the Wise Man declares.

paras.t: Quicumque aliquid tibi operatus fuerit, statim ei mercedem restitue, præsertim si petit et egeat. Qui enim fraudem facit mercenario, et qui sanguinem fundit, fratres sunt, ut in Ecclesiastico legitur. Et merces mercenarii tui apud te omnino non remaneat, hoc est diutius quam licet. Nam et unum quatuor clamitantium vitiorum, est detentio mercedis operariorum, ut Jacobus asserit. Hinc Dominus in Levitico ait: Non morabitur opus mercenarii tui apud te usque mane. Communiter enim pauperes sunt operarii tales, et indigent sua mercede.
paras.en: [[4:15|If any man hath done any work for thee, immediately pay him his hire|Quicumque aliquid tibi operatus fuerit, statim ei mercedem restitue]], above all if he asks and is in need. For [[Ecclus 34:27|He that sheddeth blood, and he that defraudeth the laborer of his hire, are brothers|Qui enim fraudem facit mercenario, et qui sanguinem fundit, fratres sunt]], as is read in Ecclesiasticus [Denis names the two in the reverse order]. [[4:15|and let not the wages of thy hired servant stay with thee at all|Et merces mercenarii tui apud te omnino non remaneat]], that is, longer than is lawful. For the withholding of labourers' wages is one of the four vices that cry out [that is, the four sins crying to heaven for vengeance], as James asserts[[Jas 5:4||]]. Hence the Lord says in Leviticus: [[Lev 19:13|The wages of him that hath been hired by thee shall not abide with thee until the morning|Non morabitur opus mercenarii tui apud te usque mane]]. For such labourers are commonly poor, and need their wages.

paras.t: Quod ab alio oderis, hoc est, rationabiliter non vis, et abhorres, fieri tibi, vide ne tu aliquando alteri facias. Duo sunt præcepta juris naturalis, unum negativum obligans semper et ad semper, quod ponitur hic; aliud affirmativum, obligans semper, sed non ad semper, quod per Matthæum exprimit Christus: Omnia, inquiens, quæcumque vultis ut faciant vobis homines, ita et vos facite illis. Quorum unum in alio includitur.
paras.en: [[4:16|what thou wouldst hate|Quod ab alio oderis]], that is, what thou dost with reason not wish and dost abhor, [[4:16|to have done to thee by another|fieri tibi]], [[4:16|See thou never do to another|vide ne tu aliquando alteri facias]]. There are two precepts of the natural law: one negative, binding always and for always, which is set down here; the other affirmative, binding always but not for always [a negative precept binds at every moment; an affirmative one is always in force, but need not be acted on at every moment], which Christ expresses through Matthew: [[Matt 7:12|All things|Omnia]], he says, [[Matt 7:12|whatsoever you would that men should do to you, do you also to them|quæcumque vultis ut faciant vobis homines, ita et vos facite illis]]. Each of them is contained in the other.

paras.t: Panem tuum cum esurientibus et egenis comede: illos invitando ut tecum manducent, sicut sanctus Job fecit, qui ait: Si comedi buccellam meam solus, et non comedit pupillus ex ea. Hinc ait Unigenitus Dei: Quum facis prandium aut cœnam, noli vocare amicos tuos, neque fratres, neque cognatos, neque vicinos divites, ne forte et ipsi te reinvitent, et fiat tibi retributio; sed quum facis convivium, voca pauperes, debiles, claudos et cæcos, et beatus eris, quia non habent retribuere tibi. Retribuetur enim tibi in resurrectione justorum. Istud consilium est, non præceptum. Et de vestimentis tuis tibi superfluis nudos tege: quemadmodum beatissimus Joannes Baptista admonuit: Qui habet duas tunicas, det non habenti; et Isaias, Quum videris nudum, operi eum. Universa etenim misericordiæ opera tempore opportuno sunt adimplenda.
paras.en: [[4:17|Eat thy bread with the hungry and the needy|Panem tuum cum esurientibus et egenis comede]]: inviting them to eat with thee, as holy Job did, who says: [[Job 31:17|If I have eaten my morsel alone, and the fatherless hath not eaten thereof|Si comedi buccellam meam solus, et non comedit pupillus ex ea]]. Hence the Only-begotten of God says: [[Luke 14:12|When thou makest a dinner or a supper, call not thy friends nor thy brethren nor thy kinsmen nor thy neighbours who are rich; lest perhaps they also invite thee again, and a recompense be made to thee|Quum facis prandium aut cœnam, noli vocare amicos tuos, neque fratres, neque cognatos, neque vicinos divites, ne forte et ipsi te reinvitent, et fiat tibi retributio]]; [[Luke 14:13|But when thou makest a feast, call the poor, the maimed, the lame and the blind|sed quum facis convivium, voca pauperes, debiles, claudos et cæcos]], [[Luke 14:14|And thou shalt be blessed, because they have not wherewith to make thee recompense: for recompense shall be made thee at the resurrection of the just|et beatus eris, quia non habent retribuere tibi. Retribuetur enim tibi in resurrectione justorum]]. This is a counsel, not a precept. [[4:17|and with thy garments|Et de vestimentis tuis]] that are more than thou needest [[4:17|cover the naked|nudos tege]]: as most blessed John the Baptist admonished, [[Luke 3:11|He that hath two coats, let him give to him that hath none|Qui habet duas tunicas, det non habenti]]; and Isaias, [[Is 58:7|when thou shalt see one naked, cover him|Quum videris nudum, operi eum]]. For all the works of mercy are to be fulfilled at the fitting time.

paras.t: Panem tuum et vinum tuum super sepulturam justi constitue, hoc est, in sepelitione fidelium refice pauperes bene pro spiritibus defunctorum in gratia. Non est autem erronee intelligendum, ut juxta quorumdam superstitionem, super monumenta mortuorum alimenta ponantur, quasi mortui corporalibus alimoniis egeant aut vescantur. De hoc recitat Augustinus in libro Confessionum, quemadmodum mater sua ad prædicationem Ambrosii, consuetudinem suam reliquerit: et quod iste sit sensus, apparet ex verbis sequentibus. Et noli ex eo manducare et bibere cum peccatoribus, hoc est incredulis, qui defunctis nequeunt suffragari.
paras.en: [[4:18|Lay out thy bread, and thy wine upon the burial of a just man|Panem tuum et vinum tuum super sepulturam justi constitue]], that is, at the burial of the faithful refresh the poor well, for the souls of those who have died in grace. It is not, however, to be wrongly understood, as though, after the superstition of some, food were to be set on the tombs of the dead, as if the dead needed or fed on bodily nourishment. Augustine tells of this in the book of the Confessions [book VI, chapter 2], how his mother gave up her custom at the preaching of Ambrose; and that this is the sense appears from the words that follow: [[4:18|and do not eat and drink thereof with the wicked|Et noli ex eo manducare et bibere cum peccatoribus]], that is, with unbelievers, who cannot help the dead by suffrages.

paras.t: Consilium semper a sapiente perquire, id est, diligenter inquire in arduis ac dubiis, in quibus ad expertorum, sapientium et Deum timentium est confugiendum consilium: quod etiam a sapientissimo Deo, et ex Scripturis ac patrum libris est inquirendum. Unde in Ecclesiastico docetur: Fili, sine consilio nihil facias, et post factum non pœnitebis.
paras.en: [[4:19|Seek counsel always of a wise man|Consilium semper a sapiente perquire]], that is, inquire diligently in hard and doubtful matters, in which one must have recourse to the counsel of the experienced, of the wise and of those who fear God; which is also to be sought from God, who is most wise, and from the Scriptures and the books of the Fathers. Hence it is taught in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 32:24|My son, do thou nothing without counsel, and thou shalt not repent when thou hast done|Fili, sine consilio nihil facias, et post factum non pœnitebis]].

paras.t: Omni tempore benedic Deum, laudando eum in prosperis et in adversis, perseveranter usque in finem, omni tempore opportuno, juxta illud in Psalmo: Benedicam Dominum in omni tempore, semper laus ejus in ore meo; et pete ab eo, ut vias, hoc est actiones tuas interiores exterioresque dirigat per se, per angelicam custodiam, per suos vicarios, atque per consiliarios bonos. Qua directione superna jugiter ac maxime indigemus, secundum illud Proverbiorum: Cor hominis disponit viam suam, sed Dei est dirigere gressus ejus. Unde sanctus ille ait Jeremias sanctificatus in utero: Scio, Domine, quia non est hominis via ejus, nec viri est, ut ambulet et dirigat gressus suos. Ideo cum Psalmista oremus: Gressus meos dirige secundum eloquium tuum. Et omnia consilia tua in ipso permaneant, ita ut nullius consilio acquiescas contra Dei præcepta ac documenta. Cuncta quoque consilia quæ inquiris, finaliter ordines, ut Deo complaceas, et salveris.
paras.en: [[4:20|Bless God at all times|Omni tempore benedic Deum]], praising him in prosperity and in adversity, perseveringly unto the end, at every fitting time, according to that in the Psalm: [[Ps 33:2|I will bless the Lord at all times, his praise shall be always in my mouth|Benedicam Dominum in omni tempore, semper laus ejus in ore meo]]; [[4:20|and desire of him to direct thy ways|et pete ab eo, ut vias]], that is, thy actions inward and outward, by himself, through the guardianship of the angels, through his vicars, and through good counsellors. Of this heavenly direction we stand continually and above all in need, according to that of Proverbs: [[Prov 16:9|The heart of man disposeth his way: but the Lord must direct his steps|Cor hominis disponit viam suam, sed Dei est dirigere gressus ejus]] [Denis reads *Dei*, of God, for *Domini*, the Lord]. Whence that holy Jeremias, who was sanctified in the womb, says: [[Jer 10:23|I know, O Lord, that the way of a man is not his: neither is it in a man to walk, and to direct his steps|Scio, Domine, quia non est hominis via ejus, nec viri est, ut ambulet et dirigat gressus suos]]. Therefore let us pray with the Psalmist: [[Ps 118:133|Direct my steps according to thy word|Gressus meos dirige secundum eloquium tuum]]. [[4:20|and that all thy counsels may abide in him|Et omnia consilia tua in ipso permaneant]], so that thou acquiesce in no one's counsel against the precepts and teachings of God. And order all the counsels thou seekest to this end, that thou mayest please God and be saved.

paras.t: Indico etiam tibi, fili mi, dedisse, hoc est concessisse, me decem talenta argenti Gabelo, etc., prout supra expositum est.
paras.en: [[4:21|I tell thee also, my son, that I lent|Indico etiam tibi, fili mi, dedisse]], that is, granted, [[4:21|ten talents of silver|me decem talenta argenti]] [[4:21|to Gabelus|Gabelo]], etc., as was explained above[[Tob 1:17||]] [the margin note here is illegible; the loan is told at Tob 1:17].

paras.t: Noli timere, fili mi, carnali, mundano, inordinato et turbulento timore. Pauperem quidem vitam gerimus in temporalibus, sed multa bona habebimus, hoc est copiosa charismata gratiæ in præsenti, bonaque gloriæ in futuro, si timuerimus Deum, filiali timore: juxta illud Psalmistæ, Timete Dominum, omnes sancti ejus, quoniam nihil deest timentibus eum; et recesserimus ab omni peccato, præsertim mortali, et etiam veniali pro posse: a quibus potissime receditur corde, ea abhorrendo: et fecerimus bene […] duas quasi integrales partes justitiæ, Propheta dicente: Declina a malo, et fac bonum, etc.
paras.en: [[4:23|Fear not, my son|Noli timere, fili mi]], with a carnal, worldly, inordinate and turbulent fear. [[4:23|we lead indeed a poor life|Pauperem quidem vitam gerimus]] in temporal things, [[4:23|but we shall have many good things|sed multa bona habebimus]], that is, abundant gifts of grace in the present, and the goods of glory in the future, [[4:23|if we fear God|si timuerimus Deum]] with a filial fear, according to that of the Psalmist, [[Ps 33:10|Fear the Lord, all ye his saints: for there is no want to them that fear him|Timete Dominum, omnes sancti ejus, quoniam nihil deest timentibus eum]] [Denis reads *nihil deest*, nothing is lacking, for *non est inopia*]; [[4:23|and depart from all sin|et recesserimus ab omni peccato]], above all mortal sin, and venial too as far as we can: from which one departs chiefly in heart, by abhorring them; [[4:23|and do that which is good|et fecerimus bene]] […] the two integral parts, as it were, of justice, as the Prophet says: [[Ps 36:27|Decline from evil and do good|Declina a malo, et fac bonum]], etc.
